density_observation: Oral/spotlight extractions are NOT denser in normative content than the chunk baseline (4.39 vs 4.36 passages/rec; 13.14 vs 12.75 signals/rec). Reject reviews show the highest density (4.99 passages, 14.28 signals) — reject reviewers articulate more weaknesses. The 'norm-rich' premise for oral/spotlight is not borne out at the aggregate level; individually the oral/spotlight examples are still high-quality reviews with explicit criteria (novelty, soundness, clarity, significance) often called out by section headers.

caveats.extraction_in_progress: Only ~88K of 259K rows in peer_review_unified.parquet have been extracted (chunk_legacy_6a7b5714ff.jsonl.gz). The oral/spotlight subset will grow as the bulk extraction proceeds; ~35% reviews currently observed (6,087 / 17,662 reviews matched).
caveats.best_papers_venue_mismatch: The 121 label=1 best papers in best_papers_v2_*.csv.gz are dominated by PLDI/CHI/INFOCOM/CVPR/SODA — venues whose reviews are NOT on OpenReview. Only BioCLIP (CVPR 2024 best paper) had an OpenReview submission to ICLR 2024, and that submission was *withdrawn* (likely sent to CVPR instead). The best_papers cross-link is therefore essentially empty (1 extraction line, parse failure). Building a useful best_papers norm-subset will require either (a) crawling reviews from PLDI/CHI/etc. tracks, (b) using PeerJ/F1000/eLife best-of lists for biology papers, or (c) treating 'oral/spotlight' as the proxy.
caveats.withdrawn_decisions: Some matched reviews come from 'Withdrawn Submission' threads (e.g. BioCLIP at ICLR), which do not reflect the eventual acceptance decision.
caveats.ok_rate: About 45% of extractions in the current chunk have ok=true (2,766/6,087 for oral/spotlight). Many of the 'not ok' are parse failures or empty passages due to Qwen generation issues.
